conviction_note: Two measurements disagree only in scale, not sign. The findings sum to +0.50: a known $0.91m IEEPA refund that should inflate headline Q1 EPS against a single-source $0.13 bar, a Walmart 1,250-store load-in scheduled for fiscal Q1, and a new Costco item (XCOR PRO 2.0, 290 warehouses from 2026-09-26) for the call. Against those sit Costco clearing the MX Pro II SE bundle at .97 markdown prices after the May load-in that made Q4, and a Q1 FY26 comparison that had its own initial Costco shipment. The scaled number is p_up 52 x abs 7.0 = +0.28. It is smaller because the revenue bar is unsourced and last quarter's EPS beat with a revenue miss traded -11.28%, so I put little weight on the EPS line.
bar: EPS $0.13 for Q1 FY27 from one source, public.com (https://public.com/stocks/axil/earnings), with no second agreeing source. Revenue consensus is UNSOURCED for Q1. Last quarter's bar was $0.16 EPS / $9.5m revenue per search snippets of benzinga/public aggregators, and actual was $0.18 / $8.56m. The company gives no guidance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001718500/000152013826000361/axil-20260818_8kex99z1.htm). Because the bar is single-source, every finding is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS: the refund alone is about $0.11 per diluted share against $0.13, and it is unknown whether the single estimate includes it.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6,016 shares as of 2026-09-15, 1.0 day to cover, about 0.1% of shares outstanding (https://equibles.com/stocks/axil/shortinterest). The December 2025 peak was 267,523. There are no listed options, so there is no skew and no priced lean. The 20-day run-up is -0.81%, the 5-day -2.23%, and the stock is 29.5% below its 52-week high. Ownership is concentrated: CEO Toghraie/Intrepid report 46.9% beneficial ownership (13D/A, 2026-08-20), and 6.82m shares are outstanding. Turnover is about $80k a day. Positioning is neither crowded short nor visibly long, so there is no squeeze mechanism.

findings.finding: The 10-K says AXIL received about $910k of IEEPA duty refunds plus interest after fiscal year-end (May 31, 2026). None of it is recognised in FY26; it is to be recorded in FY27 'as cost of revenue adjustments and other income'. Receipt was before the 2026-08-18 filing, so it falls in fiscal Q1 (Jun-Aug). That is about $0.11 per diluted share (~8.3m diluted shares implied by Q4's $1.5m / $0.18) against a $0.13 single-source EPS bar and Q1 FY26 actual EPS of $0.04, plus a gross-margin bump of roughly 10 points on a ~$8m quarter. Management already called it 'not indicative of underlying operating performance'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-08-18): EPS $0.18 beat $0.16, but revenue $8.56m missed $9.5m and the stock fell 11.28%. An EPS beat did not carry the stock when revenue missed. Q1 FY26 (2025-10-07, EPS $0.04 vs $0.02 the year before, revenue +17%): +4.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: The refund is public (8-K and 10-K, 2026-08-18), so the fact is priced. The open question is whether the one estimate behind the $0.13 bar includes it. If it did, consensus would sit near $0.20+ rather than below Q4's $0.18 on a seasonally similar quarter. A $0.13 bar suggests it may be excluded, which would show up as a headline EPS beat in a release a retail-heavy, thinly traded name will read headline-first.
findings.independence: The same fact is in the 8-K exhibit 99.1 press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001718500/000152013826000361/axil-20260818_8kex99z1.htm), which is the same company disclosure, so it counts once. The cash rise to $7.42m by 2026-08-14 (10-K) is consistent with receipt.

findings.finding: Walmart's expansion of AXIL MX PRO and MX Passive earmuffs to about 1,250 stores was announced 2026-04-29 with launch 'expected in AXIL's fiscal first quarter', so the initial stocking order falls in the June-August quarter now being reported. MCX (Marine Corps Exchange) distribution also began July 2026, in Q1. Together these are a sell-in load against a Q1 FY26 revenue comparison of $6.9m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution-driven revenue growth: Q4 FY26 +48.9% revenue on big-box orders still traded -11.28% on a miss against a $9.5m bar. Q1 FY26 +17.2% on an initial Costco shipment traded +4.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The company announced it, and the single estimate presumably models it, so this sits inside what the company told the market to expect. Filed because no one outside the company knows the size of the Walmart opening order, and it is the main positive revenue driver in the quarter.
findings.independence: The MCX start in fiscal Q1 is confirmed separately in the 2026-09-29 date-announcement release (https://finviz.com/news/396399/axil-brands-to-announce-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results-on-october-6-2026).

findings.finding: Costco is clearing the item that made AXIL's Q4. The AXIL MX Pro II SE earmuff + X30i bundle (Costco #2049073) was first seen 2026-05-11 and reached 599 warehouses, matching the 10-K's 'material orders from a big box retail chain fulfilled in the final month' of FY26 (one customer = 23% of FY26 revenue and 69% of segment AR at May 31). As of 2026-10-06 it sells at $59.97 against $99.99 at 365 of 599 warehouses, with a 60-day low of $39.97 and 39% of warehouses out of stock. Costco's .97 price ending marks a manager markdown/clearance. That points to no repeat order of comparable size in Q1 and a possible markdown allowance or return reserve against the revenue line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue against the bar is the line this name traded on last time: Q4 revenue missed $9.5m by ~10% and the stock fell 11.28% despite an EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: No analyst or aggregator tracks Costco warehouse-level pricing for a $40m-cap name with no options and ~$80k a day of turnover. If the market had seen it, the stock would have sold off after the clearance prices appeared (60-day window). Instead it is -0.81% over 20 days. Net of the rest of the company: Walmart's 1,250-store load-in and MCX (finding 2) land in the same quarter and could fully offset a missing Costco reorder. The segment is 96% of revenue, so this one customer is roughly a quarter of it. Sized as a proxy, below what a document would earn.
findings.independence: Proxy. The 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1718500/000152013826000360/axil-20260531_10k.htm) independently confirms that a big-box load-in landed in May 2026 and was a one-customer concentration. It does not confirm whether that customer reordered in Q1.

findings.finding: Costco has picked up a new AXIL item. AXIL XCOR PRO 2.0 Bluetooth hearing earbuds (Costco #2088417, $119.99, stable price) were first spotted 2026-09-26 and are now stocked at 290 warehouses, 53% in stock and 47% low stock. That points to a fresh Costco purchase order shipped around late August/September, which is fiscal Q2 and material for what management says on tonight's call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AXIL gives no formal guidance. Its best reaction in the baseline (+15.56%, 2026-01-08) and its +4.25% on 2025-10-07 both came on prints that announced retail-channel expansion (Costco, Walmart).
findings.why_not_priced: The company has not issued a release about this Costco order. The 2026-09-29 release mentions only MCX. A known Costco rotation into a $119.99 item across ~290 warehouses would be visible as a pre-print bid in a thin stock, and the 5-day run-up is -2.23%. Whether it shipped in late August (Q1) or September (Q2) is unknown, so it is filed against the call commentary rather than the quarter.
findings.independence: Shares the same tracker as finding 3 but is a different item and a different direction; read together they describe Costco rotating items, not exiting. The earlier XCOR SE was in 300+ Costco stores (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/34683535/axil-brands-launches-nationwide-at-costco-with-axil-xcor-se-advanced-hearing-protection-and-enhancement-earbuds), which shows a repeat pattern.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY26 comparison carries its own load-in. Q1 FY26 revenue of $6.9m (+17.2%) was driven by the 'initial shipment of our AXIL hearing products to a new national membership-based retail chain', so year-on-year growth in Q1 FY27 compares against a quarter that already held a Costco opening order.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 itself traded +4.25% on that 17% growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a year. Filed small because a y/y growth headline below Q4's +48.9% may read as a deceleration to retail holders anchored on the Q4 headline, and no preview addresses the comparison base.

findings.finding: Cash rose to about $7.42m at 2026-08-14 from $4.5m at May 31, with no borrowings. The 10-K says the big-box receivable was 'substantially collected' and the $0.91m refund received, so Q1 operating cash flow will show the Q4 working-capital build reversing. There is no ATM, S-3 or buyback.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed. Q4's negative operating cash flow ($-9.6k FY26) was disclosed alongside the -11.28% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-K, so mostly priced. It reaches the balance sheet only in tonight's release.
findings.independence: Shares the 10-K with finding 1; the cash figure partly includes the refund.

outside_window.finding: A voting agreement and irrevocable proxy gives Intrepid (CEO Toghraie) control over Don Vasquez's 1,276,251 shares (18.7%) and expires 2026-10-17. After that, an 18.7% holder regains free voting and disposition, which in a stock trading ~13k shares a day is a potential overhang.
Reviv3 hair and skin care relaunch planned for September 2026. The segment is 4% of revenue ($1.19m FY26, -21.9%), so its numbers land in Q2.

searched_and_found_nothing: Q1 FY27 revenue consensus: benzinga (403), chartmill (403), zacks (bot wall), fxempire (dashes), marketbeat (wrong page), stockanalysis (404), alphaquery (503). Only public.com gave EPS $0.13.
EDGAR since 2026-08-18: only the 10-K, the 8-K and a 13D/A (2026-08-20, share-count update with no transactions). No 8-K, S-3, Form 4 cluster or financing.
Company news since August: only the 2026-09-29 date announcement (MCX in Q1). No XCOR 2.0 or Reviv3 relaunch release found.
Walmart in-store/online availability for MX PRO / MX Passive: no third-party tracker data found.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Short-interest decline from 267,523 shares (Dec 2025) to 6,016 (Sept 2026) as a positioning signal
rejected_candidates.detail: Recorded in positioning_check rather than as a finding. It is ~0.1% of shares outstanding, so it gives no squeeze or crowding mechanism either way.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew. The flat 20-day run-up (-0.81%) and the 29% drawdown from the high give no directional lean, so the findings do not fight a priced lean. They are roughly balanced: an EPS headline helped by the refund against a revenue line exposed to a missing Costco reorder.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): refund finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8. It lands below underlying operations, the company flagged it as not indicative, and last quarter's EPS beat with a revenue miss traded -11.28%.
Rule 6 (inside what was guided/announced): Walmart Q1 load-in cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because the company announced it for fiscal Q1.
Rule 5 (proxy) and rule 9 (net of the rest): Costco clearance cut from -1.5 to -1.2, net of the Walmart/MCX load-in in the same quarter. Kept filed as a proxy.
Rule 6 (single-source bar): XCOR PRO 2.0 cut from +1.0 to +0.8 and the comparison-base finding from -0.5 to -0.3; every finding stays capped small.
Rule 8 (thin coverage): abs_move_pct kept at 7.0, above the 5.16 median; not shrunk for sign uncertainty.
Cash finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1 (shares the 10-K with the refund finding).
